title: stochastic-fallback-admitter-for-continuous-batcher-starvation-mitigation
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Production traffic patterns exposed intermittent starvation of KV-heavy requests in continuous-batch workers when a small number of long-lived KV-pin flows monopolized slots. This caused tail latency spikes under moderate load even though median throughput was fine. Motivation: Introduce a lightweight runtime admission policy that probabilistically relaxes strict slot reservations and induces controlled fallbacks to non-prefetch paths for dominated flows, reducing starvation without regressing steady-state throughput. Design summary: add a StochasticFallbackAdmitter that observes per-slot hold durations and per-flow KV-saturation score, computes a time-decayed weight, and performs a small-probability fallback decision when a scorer exceeds a runtime-configurable threshold. The admitter is integrated into the continuous-batcher admission path with two knobs: fallback_probability_base and aging_half_life_ms. It also supports a strict-mode toggle for canary rollout (strict-mode=false uses probabilistic fallbacks; strict-mode=true is no-op). Key goals: reduce P99 latency for short requests co-located with KV-heavy flows, avoid deterministic preemption that causes jitter, keep overhead <1% CPU on typical workers, and be togglable via runtime flags/feature gates. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (internal: ENG-2345) [x] unit tests for scorer math and config parsing [x] integration test for deterministic behavior under synthetic KV-heavy load [x] perf benchmark harness for mixed workloads [x] rolling canary plan and playbook updates Implementation notes: - New files: serving/batcher/admitters/stochastic_fallback_admitter.{cc,h} and serving/batcher/admitters/README.md describing heuristics; minor changes to serving/batcher/continuous_batcher.cc to invoke the admitter; metrics exported via observability/metrics_registry.cc (stochastic_fallback_evaluations, stochastic_fallback_taken). - KV cache interaction: rather than evicting pins, the admitter requests a fallback path which avoids prefetch/KV-pin optimization for the specific request; this preserves overall cache health while reducing slot hold time. - Kernel-level changes: no kernel changes; we only add admission logic at the batching layer to avoid risky low-level regressions. - Rollout: default disabled; enabled as opt-in on canary fleet, then ramped using rollout heuristics in docs/ops/rollout.md. Commits summary: ["init: implement stochastic fallback admitter skeleton", "impl: scorer + time-decay math and config parsing", "hook: wire admitter into continuous batcher admission path", "metrics: add observability counters and alerting guidance", "test: unit+integration+perf harness updates", "docs: add rollout playbook and feature flag notes"] Changed areas/files: ["serving/batcher/admitters/stochastic_fallback_admitter.cc", "serving/batcher/admitters/stochastic_fallback_admitter.h", "serving/batcher/continuous_batcher.cc", "observability/metrics_registry.cc", "tests/integration/kv_fallback_integration_test.cc", "benchmarks/continuous_batcher/mixed_kv_sweep.yml", "docs/ops/rollout.md"] Tests and performance: on the internal perf harness (mixed 80% short text gen, 20% long KV-pin flows), enabling probabilistic fallbacks at fallback_probability_base=0.05 and aging_half_life_ms=60000 reduced client-observed P99 latency for short requests by ~36% (120ms -> 77ms) while increasing median token CPU by 0.5% and end-to-end throughput change within noise (+0.8%). Tail improvement came with a small increase in observed cache miss-rate for the fallback cohort (expected). CI: linux-unit-tests (pass), integration-kv (pass), benchmark-smoke (pass), lint (pass), security-scan (pass). Review convo highlights: reviewer Samir: "Looks good; can we quantify worst-case extra load on backend KV service when fallback flips many requests?" Author reply: "Bench shows 0.8% throughput delta and cache miss-rate uptick limited to fallback cohort; added grafana dashboard panel and alert guidance in docs/ops/rollout.md." Reviewer Claire: "Please add safety gate so fallback_probability_base cannot exceed 0.2 in production by config schema." Author update: "Added max_allowed_probability cap and schema validation; updated unit tests." Reviewer Elena: "Add note on interaction with canary prefetch warmups and dedicated pools." Author reply: "Documented and added a check in admitter to avoid fallbacks for requests marked as critical-prefetch." Merge: After two approvals and passing CI, PR was squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-25. Rollout: started on 2026-02-26 targeted canary fleet 5% then 25% with careful alerting on cache miss-rate and backend QPS. Post-merge followups: ENG-2560 (observability dashboard tweaks), ENG-2598 (adaptive fallback tuning based on backend QPS), and a planned RFC to explore deterministic-mini-preempt strategy if stochastic approach underperforms in specific tenants.

release_notes: Added a Stochastic Fallback Admitter for continuous batcher to reduce starvation in KV-heavy co-located workloads; opt-in via feature flag and runtime configs; improves P99 latency for short requests with minimal throughput impact; rollout begins on canary fleet; see docs/ops/rollout.md for playbook and observability guidance.
notes: This PR focuses solely on admission-layer behavior and avoids kernel or low-level runtime changes to minimize regression blast radius. Follow-ups will explore adaptive tuning that reacts to backend QPS.
